title: Amazon Science researchers combine optimization techniques to improve LLM performance
excerpt: The integration of knowledge distillation and Medusa-2 produced a model matching the quality of a 70-billion-parameter teacher at higher speeds.
bodyHtml:
Amazon Science announced on October 29, 2026, that combining knowledge distillation and the Medusa-2 framework improves the speed and cost effectiveness of large language models. Knowledge distillation is a compression technique where a powerful model produces training targets for a lightweight model. Medusa is a framework that transforms sequential next-token predictions into parallel computations.

In collaboration with Booking.com, researchers applied these techniques to three use cases. The resulting 1.1-billion-parameter TinyLlama model matched the quality of the 70-billion-parameter Llama-3.1 teacher while running 10 to 20 times as fast. For the AI Trip Planner, the pipeline drove a 2.9% increase in user engagement compared to GPT-3.5.

The team also reported that accommodation description generation saw 1.4% more helpful ratings at lower costs than other models. Additionally, for Smart Filters, the approach delivered responses 15 times as fast for 99% of queries. These techniques were presented at the meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, where the work received the Industry Track best-paper award.
